jobs.title: Senior Director, AI Architecture
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

This leader sets one standard way to build, secure and run AI across RBC Technology & Operations. They own the reference architecture for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), AI agents, model access and AI-native software delivery (AI-DLC). The role turns the 2030 T&O ambitions, including AI-native delivery and 30% of GenAI volume on open-weight models, into patterns teams actually use.

Success means fewer bespoke stacks, faster delivery with maintainable code, and AI that Internal Audit, Model Risk and OSFI can trust.

What will you do
?

AI architecture standards as code. Define the enterprise AI reference architecture and approved patterns. Encode them as harness skills, agent constitutions and automated fitness checks, so standards apply at generation time rather than at review.
Common RAG substrate. Converge the many RAG solutions onto one shared platform: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, reranking and evaluation. Retrieval must respect source entitlements by default. Set a retirement plan for duplicate stacks.
Agent sandboxing and security architecture. Design the sandbox standard for every agentic workload: ephemeral environments, egress allow-lists, short-lived task-scoped credentials and no standing production access. Own agent identity, tool access through a governed MCP gateway and registry, and defenses against prompt injection and poisoned tools.
AI-DLC harness and quality gates. Own the harness architecture from spec to release. Make quality gates deterministic and mandatory: tests and coverage, static analysis, complexity and duplication limits, dependency and license checks, security scanning and architecture fitness checks. Enforce separation of duties (the agent that writes a change cannot approve it), PR size limits and traceability from spec to deployment.
Skills and evaluation lifecycle. Treat skills like code: owned, versioned, regression-tested with evals and retired when stale. Re-run evals before any model upgrade reaches teams.
Model gateway and inference architecture. Route work across frontier and open-weight models by cost, risk and jurisdiction. Build in token metering, caching and data-classification rules so cost and residency are enforced by the platform.
Risk-tiered control model. Partner with Internal Audit, Model Risk and Cyber to define human-oversight tiers, from human-on-the-loop for low-risk work to human-in-the-loop for payments and core banking. Align with OSFI Guidelines E-23 and B-13.
Design authority and innovation. Chair AI architecture review, keep decision records and manage exceptions. Graduate proven lab work into the platform and evaluate emerging technology, such as agent protocols and new open-weight models.

What do you need to succeed?

15+ years in architecture or engineering, including 5+ years leading architects or engineers at enterprise scale.
Hands-on depth in LLM systems: RAG, agent frameworks, MCP, evaluation and inference serving on cloud and on-premises GPUs.
Security architecture for AI, including the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications, sandboxing and identity for non-human actors.
Strong DevSecOps and SDLC background; you have shipped quality gates engineers accepted rather than routed around.
Experience in a regulated industry, ideally financial services under OSFI.
Credibility with engineers: you still prototype and read code. Able to explain trade-offs plainly to executives and audit.

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable

Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
A world-class training program in financial services

jobs.title: Senior Director, Data Architecture & Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

The Senior Director, Data Architecture simplifies and unifies RBC's data architecture across the full lifecycle: manufacturing, distribution, discovery, consumption and governance. They own the target data architecture and the standards that make data machine-readable for AI agents and operate the architecture function with agents as a core part of how it works. Success means fewer data stores and point-to-point feeds, one trusted source for each critical data element, and data products agents can find and use within their entitlements.

Key pillars of this role:

Agent Assisted Architecture operations: Run continuous inventory of data platforms and stores across RBC’s stacks. Deploy automated architecture review and decision record workflows powered by agents to scale governance and documentation
Agent governance and trust: Establish audit trails of agent data access tied to entitlements. Implement evals to validate whether agents can answer correctly from data products. Define human-in-the-loop thresholds and ensure agents meet regulatory expectations for auditability and transparency

What will you do?

Manufacturing (data sources): Name the authoritative source for every critical data element. Own the canonical data model and business glossary alignment. Set the standard for producer data contracts covering schema, semantics, quality rules and SLAs, so quality is fixed at the source. Establish feedback loops where agent usage and failures feedback to producers-if agents can't interpret a field, that becomes a defect against the source.
Distribution (data platform architecture): Contribute to data distribution platform architecture and the standard ingestion patterns: batch, streaming, CDC, events and APIs. Move data once, reliably and traceably. Operate a roadmap to retire point-to-point interfaces.
Agent-assisted architecture operations: Run continuous inventory of data platforms and stores across RBC's stacks. Deploy automated architecture review and decision record workflows powered by agents. Enable agents to assist in architecture assessment, governance documentation, and exception tracking at scale.
Discovery and machine readability: Define what counts as a data product and the minimum metadata each must carry: meaning, owner, lineage, quality and entitlements. Build the semantic layer and ontology that lets agents interpret data, not just locate it. Set the agent-access pattern for data products, such as MCP. Include unstructured data (documents, emails, call transcripts) with appropriate chunking, embeddings and freshness strategies so retrieval-augmented workflows have high-quality context.
Consumption: Define the consumption archetypes (BI, operational APIs, analytics and ML, RAG, agents) with one supported pattern for each. Feed curated, entitlement-aware data products into the common RAG substrate.
Agent governance and trust: Design and implement evals for data products to validate whether agents can answer correctly from them. Establish audit trails of agent data access tied to entitlements. Define human-in-the-loop thresholds and escalation patterns. Align with model-risk governance frameworks (OSFI E-23) to ensure agents operating on data products meet regulatory expectations for transparency and auditability.
Governance by design: Act as design authority through architecture review, decision records and exceptions. Partner with the CDO, who owns policy and accountability, while this role owns how standards are built in. Support regulatory lineage and jurisdiction-aware data placement for sovereignty.
Data quality for retrieval: Establish quality standards and practices specific to retrieval scenarios: chunking strategies, freshness SLAs, embedding quality, and unstructured data preparation (documents, emails, call transcripts). Ensure that data products used in RAG and agent workflows meet standards for accuracy and interpretability.
Simplification and transformation: Inventory data platforms, stores and tools across RBC's stacks and give each a disposition: tolerate, invest, migrate or eliminate. Tie the roadmap to in-flight programs such as Finance Modernization and AML Transformation, and to third-party rationalization. Track and communicate measurable outcomes: machine-readability coverage (% of critical data elements with semantics, owner, lineage and entitlements), agent task success rates on data products, and time-to-onboard new data products.
Build/buy stance on the agent layer: Establish strategy and standards for agent infrastructure: gateway and routing, tool registry for data product access, and shared context or memory layers. Make principled decisions on build versus buy for agent-specific data infrastructure.

What do you need to succeed?

15+ years in data architecture or data engineering, including 5+ years leading architects at enterprise scale.
Depth across lakehouse and warehouse platforms, streaming and CDC, data products and mesh, catalogs and metadata, semantic layers and knowledge graphs.
A track record of measurable simplification and modernization: data feeds rationalized, costs reduced, machine-readability coverage improved and agent task success rates on data products demonstrated.
Working knowledge of regulatory frameworks including BCBS 239, privacy regulation, OSFI E-23 (model risk) and OSFI expectations for data risk.
Clear view on making data AI-ready for retrieval, entitlement propagation, agent access and unstructured data workflows.
Experience designing and implementing data product governance, metadata standards and agent-accessible data architectures.
Able to align the CDO, platform engineering, business data owners and AI/ML leadership without direct authority over them.

What's in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

AI & Data Consulting | Office Leadership & Growth

Calgary, AB (Hybrid)
Full-time, permanent position

Opportunity to establish and lead a new Calgary office

Raise has partnered with a growing, AI-first data and engineering consulting firm that helps mid-market and enterprise organizations leverage Generative AI, Agentic AI, data analytics, and intelligent automation to solve complex business challenges and drive measurable results.

Combining deep business expertise with modern technology platforms, our client delivers practical, scalable solutions that create meaningful business impact.

Now, they're looking for someone to build and lead their Calgary operation.

This is a unique opportunity for an experienced technology consulting professional who brings together technical expertise, proven people leadership, strategic thinking, and strong client relationships.

We're looking for someone who understands what it takes to build a successful consulting business, from developing a thoughtful market strategy and recruiting the right talent to leading client engagements and establishing a high-performing local team.

This is not a traditional sales or business development role.

Success requires more than an established network or the ability to generate new business. You'll need the technical credibility to engage directly in client solution discussions, the leadership experience to build and manage a team, and the strategic mindset to turn a new market opportunity into a sustainable business.

You'll work directly with the founders and executive leadership, with significant autonomy and accountability for establishing the Calgary office and shaping its long-term success.

Whether you've previously helped build a practice or are ready to take the next step into broader business leadership, this is an opportunity to make a tangible impact.

What You'll Be Doing

Client Relationships & Market Strategy

Build and maintain trusted, long-term relationships with senior executives and business leaders across Calgary's business community.
Develop a clear, actionable go-to-market strategy that identifies target industries, priority accounts, service opportunities, and measurable growth objectives.
Establish strategic partnerships and build credibility within Calgary's technology and business communities.
Identify opportunities to expand client relationships while maintaining accountability for service quality and successful delivery.

Office Development, Planning & Operations

We're looking for a well-rounded consulting leader who can see the big picture while understanding what it takes to execute.

Someone who can build strong relationships with executive stakeholders, confidently participate in technical discussions, and lead a team through the successful delivery of complex consulting engagements.

Rather than inheriting an existing team and predetermined business model, you'll have the opportunity to shape the Calgary operation, from its market strategy and client relationships to its hiring priorities and consulting capabilities.
